Your operators already have a CODESYS screen. Export it from the IDE, import it
into HotLoop, and it opens as a HotLoop screen on the same PLC's variables. This
is the way off WebVisu: the PLC keeps running its program, HotLoop reads it
through the OPC UA connector, and the screen is HotLoop's. HotLoop for CODESYS
runs the Edge, so this is its import too.

## Use it

In the CODESYS IDE, select the visualization in the project tree and use
**Project, Export** (the CODESYS native export, a `.export` file). Not
**Export PLCopenXML**: that file has no visualization in it, and HotLoop says so
if you pick it.

On the Dashboards screen, **Import**, choose the `.export` file, **Read the
file**. It tells you:

* the visualization it found (a file with several asks you which),
* every tag the screen reads that this install does not have. The variables
  arrive as `plc/<GVL>.<variable>`: map the device `plc` to the HotLoop device
  the PLC is on and every tag moves at once, or map the tags one by one,
* **worth a look**: every element it could not put on the screen, with the
  reason, before anything is saved.

Nothing is saved until nothing is in the way. Importing needs
`dashboards.write`, and a button or a setpoint on a tag that is not marked
writable is refused here, the same as a build, so the screen never has a control
the gate would turn down.

Through the API it is `POST /api/dashboards/import` with `codesys` (the text of
the file) in place of `file`, and `visualization` to name one of several:

```json
{"codesys": "<ExportFile>...", "visualization": "Overview", "dryRun": true,
 "remap": {"devices": {"plc": "line-3"}}}
```

The report has the usual `problems`, `warnings` and `remapped`, and a
`conversion` with `mapped` (each element and what it became) and `unmapped`
(each element and why not).

## What comes across

| CODESYS element | In HotLoop |
|---|---|
| Rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse with text and a variable (`Temperature: %2.1f C`) | a readout: the variable's tag, the text before it as the caption, the text after it as the unit, the decimals from the format |
| The same with text and no variable | a label |
| Lamp | a lamp, lit by the variable, colored from the lamp's own color (red is a fault, yellow a warning, blue information, anything else a run lamp). `NOT x` reads the tag the other way up |
| Meter, potentiometer | a readout of the variable. A knob that set a value also gets a setpoint card with the dial's scale as its limits |
| Rocker switch, toggle, push button | a lamp showing the state, and a button card: on and off for a toggle, the one value for a tap |
| Polygon, polyline, and shapes with no text and no variable (the pipes, the vessel, the frames) | the picture behind the symbols, drawn from their points and colors |
| Group | its members, placed from the group's corner |

Every element keeps its pixel place: the page is the symbols card, drawn as one
scaled picture, so the screen holds its shape at any size and on a phone.

## What does not come across

Said in the import, one line each, never dropped quietly:

* an element type with no HotLoop symbol (a trace, a table, a slider, an image
  element, and the rest of the toolbox),
* a variable that is an expression (`Temp * 2`, `a AND b`, an array element):
  HotLoop shows a tag, so add a tag for the expression and point a readout at it,
* a visibility, color or movement rule driven by a PLC value: the symbol is
  there all the time and does not change color,
* a bezier curve is drawn as straight lines between its points, and a rotated
  element is not rotated,
* the page size, which the export does not hold: the page is as big as the
  outermost element, plus a margin,
* text longer than 40 characters is cut, and the dials are numbers, not dials.

The text styles, fonts and colors of the CODESYS style are HotLoop's: the screen
follows HotLoop's theme.

## How it reads the file

CODESYS documents that the native export exists and is XML, and does not document
what is in it. The reader here follows what the IDE itself writes (CODESYS 3.5
SP22, Visualization 4.10): every element stores its settings as a list of
numbered members, and the number is the CRC-32 of the member's path in the
element's description, such as `m_StaticPosition.iX`, which the IDE installs next
to itself. The tests hold values read from the IDE's own export. A setting that
carries a variable and is not read is reported as above, so a screen is never
imported as complete when it is not.

## The next step

Open the screen, check the readouts against the plant, and put the setpoint and
button cards where your operators expect them. A screen you built by hand and a
screen you imported are the same thing from here: it exports as a
[screen file](/iot/screen-file/), versions with every save, and goes to another
install the same way.
